v: Paul and Timothy, servants[^1] of Christ Jesus,[^2] to all God's holy people[^3] in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, together with the overseers[^4] and deacons:[^5]
Παῦλος καὶ Τιμόθεος δοῦλοι Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Φιλίπποις σὺν ἐπισκόποις καὶ διακόνοις·
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
I thank my God every time I remember you,[^6]
Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ μνείᾳ ὑμῶν
always in every prayer of mine for all of you, praying with joy,
πάντοτε ἐν πάσῃ δεήσει μου ὑπὲρ πάντων ὑμῶν, μετὰ χαρᾶς τὴν δέησιν ποιούμενος,
because of your partnership[^7] in the good news from the first day until now.
ἐπὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἀπὸ τῆς πρώτης ἡμέρας ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν,
I am confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.
πεποιθὼς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ὅτι ὁ ἐναρξάμενος ἐν ὑμῖν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐπιτελέσει ἄχρι ἡμέρας Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ·
It is right for me to think this way about all of you, because I have you in my heart,[^8] since both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the good news you all share with me in grace.

καθώς ἐστιν δίκαιον ἐμοὶ τοῦτο φρονεῖν ὑπὲρ πάντων ὑμῶν, διὰ τὸ ἔχειν με ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμᾶς, ἔν τε τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀπολογίᾳ καὶ βεβαιώσει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου συγκοινωνούς μου τῆς χάριτος πάντας ὑμᾶς ὄντας·
For God is my witness how I long for all of you with the affection[^9] of Christ Jesus.
μάρτυς γάρ μου ὁ θεός, ὡς ἐπιποθῶ πάντας ὑμᾶς ἐν σπλάγχνοις Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
And this is my prayer: that your love may overflow more and more in knowledge and all insight,
καὶ τοῦτο προσεύχομαι ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ὑμῶν ἔτι μᾶλλον καὶ μᾶλλον περισσεύῃ ἐν ἐπιγνώσει καὶ πάσῃ αἰσθήσει,
so that you may approve what is excellent,[^10] and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ,
εἰς τὸ δοκιμάζειν ὑμᾶς τὰ διαφέροντα, ἵνα ἦτε εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀπρόσκοποι εἰς ἡμέραν Χριστοῦ,
filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
πεπληρωμένοι καρπὸν δικαιοσύνης τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς δόξαν καὶ ἔπαινον θεοῦ.
I want you to know, brothers and sisters,[^11] that what has happened to me has actually served to advance the good news,
Γινώσκειν δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι τὰ κατʼ ἐμὲ μᾶλλον εἰς προκοπὴν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐλήλυθεν,
so that it has become clear throughout the whole praetorian guard[^12] and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ.[^13]
ὥστε τοὺς δεσμούς μου φανεροὺς ἐν Χριστῷ γενέσθαι ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ πραιτωρίῳ καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς πᾶσιν,
And most of the brothers and sisters, made confident in the Lord by my chains,[^14] are much more bold to speak the word[^15] without fear.
καὶ τοὺς πλείονας τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἐν κυρίῳ πεποιθότας τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου περισσοτέρως τολμᾶν ἀφόβως τὸν λόγον λαλεῖν.
Some, it is true, proclaim Christ even from envy and rivalry, but others from goodwill.
Τινὲς μὲν καὶ διὰ φθόνον καὶ ἔριν, τινὲς δὲ καὶ διʼ εὐδοκίαν τὸν Χριστὸν κηρύσσουσιν·
These do it out of love, knowing that I am put here for the defense of the good news.[^16]
οἱ μὲν ἐξ ἀγάπης, εἰδότες ὅτι εἰς ἀπολογίαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου κεῖμαι,
The others proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition,[^17] not sincerely, thinking they will stir up trouble for me in my chains.
οἱ δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας τὸν Χριστὸν καταγγέλλουσιν, οὐχ ἁγνῶς, οἰόμενοι θλῖψιν ἐγείρειν τοῖς δεσμοῖς μου.
What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will rejoice,
τί γάρ; πλὴν ὅτι παντὶ τρόπῳ, εἴτε προφάσει εἴτε ἀληθείᾳ, Χριστὸς καταγγέλλεται, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ χαίρω· ἀλλὰ καὶ χαρήσομαι,
for I know that through your prayers and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ this will turn out for my deliverance,[^18]
οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι τοῦτό μοι ἀποβήσεται εἰς σωτηρίαν διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν δεήσεως καὶ ἐπιχορηγίας τοῦ πνεύματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
according to my eager expectation and hope that I will not be put to shame in anything, but that with all boldness, now as always, Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death.
κατὰ τὴν ἀποκαραδοκίαν καὶ ἐλπίδα μου ὅτι ἐν οὐδενὶ αἰσχυνθήσομαι, ἀλλʼ ἐν πάσῃ παρρησίᾳ ὡς πάντοτε καὶ νῦν μεγαλυνθήσεται Χριστὸς ἐν τῷ σώματί μου, εἴτε διὰ ζωῆς εἴτε διὰ θανάτου.
For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
ἐμοὶ γὰρ τὸ ζῆν Χριστὸς καὶ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν κέρδος.
But if I am to live in the flesh,[^19] that means fruitful work for me. Yet which I will choose I cannot say.[^20]
εἰ δὲ τὸ ζῆν ἐν σαρκί, τοῦτό μοι καρπὸς ἔργου— καὶ τί αἱρήσομαι οὐ γνωρίζω·
I am torn between the two. My desire is to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better,
συνέχομαι δὲ ἐκ τῶν δύο, τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν ἔχων εἰς τὸ ἀναλῦσαι καὶ σὺν Χριστῷ εἶναι, πολλῷ γὰρ μᾶλλον κρεῖσσον,
but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
τὸ δὲ ἐπιμένειν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ἀναγκαιότερον διʼ ὑμᾶς.
Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith,
καὶ τοῦτο πεποιθὼς οἶδα ὅτι μενῶ καὶ παραμενῶ πᾶσιν ὑμῖν εἰς τὴν ὑμῶν προκοπὴν καὶ χαρὰν τῆς πίστεως,
so that your boasting in Christ Jesus may overflow because of me, through my coming[^21] to you again.
ἵνα τὸ καύχημα ὑμῶν περισσεύῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ διὰ τῆς ἐμῆς παρουσίας πάλιν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

Only, live as citizens[^22] worthy of the good news of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear about you that you are standing firm in one spirit, with one mind[^23] striving side by side for the faith of the good news,
Μόνον ἀξίως τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ Χριστοῦ πολιτεύεσθε, ἵνα εἴτε ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ὑμᾶς εἴτε ἀπὼν ἀκούω τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν, ὅτι στήκετε ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι, μιᾷ ψυχῇ συναθλοῦντες τῇ πίστει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου,
and that you are not frightened in any way by your opponents. (This is a sign to them of destruction, but of your salvation, and that from God.
καὶ μὴ πτυρόμενοι ἐν μηδενὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀντικειμένων (ἥτις ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς ἔνδειξις ἀπωλείας, ὑμῶν δὲ σωτηρίας, καὶ τοῦτο ἀπὸ θεοῦ,
For it has been granted to you, for the sake of Christ, not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him.)
ὅτι ὑμῖν ἐχαρίσθη τὸ ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, οὐ μόνον τὸ εἰς αὐτὸν πιστεύειν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πάσχειν),
You are engaged in the same struggle that you saw I had and now hear that I have.
τὸν αὐτὸν ἀγῶνα ἔχοντες οἷον εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοὶ καὶ νῦν ἀκούετε ἐν ἐμοί.

n.2: *Christ*: Greek *Christos*, "anointed one", the Greek equivalent of "Messiah". In Paul's letters it usually works as a name, so this translation writes "Christ". Paul's order, "Christ Jesus" or "Jesus Christ", is kept as the Greek has it.
n.5: Greek *diakonoi*, "servants", here used of people holding a recognized role in the church; traditionally "deacons".
n.6: Or "for all your remembrance of me". Literally "at all the remembrance of you".
n.8: Or "because you have me in your heart".
n.9: Literally "with the inward parts", the seat of the deepest feelings.
n.10: Or "discern what matters". Literally "test the things that differ".
n.11: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike; also in verse 14.
n.12: Greek *praitorion*, the emperor's guard, or the headquarters of a governor.
n.13: Literally "that my chains have become evident in Christ".
n.14: Or "most of the brothers and sisters in the Lord, made confident by my chains".
n.15: Some manuscripts read "the word of God".
n.16: Many manuscripts have verses 16 and 17 in the reverse order.
n.18: Or "salvation". The words "this will turn out for my deliverance" are the same as Job 13:16 in the Septuagint.
n.19: That is, in the body; also in verse 24.
n.20: The Greek is abrupt; literally "But if to live in the flesh, this for me is fruit of work; and what I will choose I do not make known."
n.22: Greek *politeuomai*, "to live as a citizen". Philippi was a Roman colony, and many of its people were Roman citizens.
n.23: Literally "with one soul". *In one spirit*: or "in one Spirit".

v: So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit,[^1] any affection and compassion,
Εἴ τις οὖν παράκλησις ἐν Χριστῷ, εἴ τι παραμύθιον ἀγάπης, εἴ τις κοινωνία πνεύματος, εἴ τις σπλάγχνα καὶ οἰκτιρμοί,
make my joy complete by being of the same mind, having the same love, being one in spirit[^2] and of one mind.
πληρώσατέ μου τὴν χαρὰν ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ φρονῆτε, τὴν αὐτὴν ἀγάπην ἔχοντες, σύμψυχοι, τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες,
Do nothing out of selfish ambition[^3] or conceit,[^4] but in humility regard others as more important than yourselves,
μηδὲν κατʼ ἐριθείαν μηδὲ κατὰ κενοδοξίαν, ἀλλὰ τῇ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ ἀλλήλους ἡγούμενοι ὑπερέχοντας ἑαυτῶν,
each of you looking not only to your own interests but also to the interests of others.[^5]
μὴ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἕκαστοι σκοποῦντες, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἑτέρων ἕκαστοι.
Have this attitude among yourselves, which was also in Christ Jesus:[^6]
τοῦτο φρονεῖτε ἐν ὑμῖν ὃ καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,
who, being in the form[^7] of God,[^8] did not regard equality with God as something to be grasped,[^9]
ὃς ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὑπάρχων οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγήσατο τὸ εἶναι ἴσα θεῷ,
but emptied himself,[^10] taking the form of a servant,[^11] being made in human likeness. And being found in appearance as a human being,
ἀλλὰ ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσεν μορφὴν δούλου λαβών, ἐν ὁμοιώματι ἀνθρώπων γενόμενος· καὶ σχήματι εὑρεθεὶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος
he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.
ἐταπείνωσεν ἑαυτὸν γενόμενος ὑπήκοος μέχρι θανάτου, θανάτου δὲ σταυροῦ·
Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name,
διὸ καὶ ὁ θεὸς αὐτὸν ὑπερύψωσεν, καὶ ἐχαρίσατο αὐτῷ τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα,
so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
ἵνα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ πᾶν γόνυ κάμψῃ ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ καταχθονίων,
and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord,[^12] to the glory of God the Father.
καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσηται ὅτι κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ πατρός.
So then, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only as in my presence[^13] but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
Ὥστε, ἀγαπητοί μου, καθὼς πάντοτε ὑπηκούσατε, μὴ ὡς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ μου μόνον ἀλλὰ νῦν πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐν τῇ ἀπουσίᾳ μου, μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου τὴν ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίαν κατεργάζεσθε,
for it is God who is at work in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure.[^14]
θεὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐνεργῶν ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐδοκίας.
Do everything without grumbling or arguing,
Πάντα ποιεῖτε χωρὶς γογγυσμῶν καὶ διαλογισμῶν,
so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without fault in the midst of a crooked and twisted generation,[^15] among whom you shine like lights[^16] in the world,
ἵνα γένησθε ἄμεμπτοι καὶ ἀκέραιοι, τέκνα θεοῦ ἄμωμα μέσον γενεᾶς σκολιᾶς καὶ διεστραμμένης, ἐν οἷς φαίνεσθε ὡς φωστῆρες ἐν κόσμῳ
holding fast[^17] the word of life, so that I may have reason to boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
λόγον ζωῆς ἐπέχοντες, εἰς καύχημα ἐμοὶ εἰς ἡμέραν Χριστοῦ, ὅτι οὐκ εἰς κενὸν ἔδραμον οὐδὲ εἰς κενὸν ἐκοπίασα.
But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service[^18] of your faith, I rejoice, and I rejoice with all of you.
ἀλλὰ εἰ καὶ σπένδομαι ἐπὶ τῇ θυσίᾳ καὶ λειτουργίᾳ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν, χαίρω καὶ συγχαίρω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν·
In the same way you too should rejoice, and rejoice with me.
τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ καὶ ὑμεῖς χαίρετε καὶ συγχαίρετέ μοι.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be cheered when I learn how you are.
Ἐλπίζω δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Τιμόθεον ταχέως πέμψαι ὑμῖν, ἵνα κἀγὼ εὐψυχῶ γνοὺς τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν.
For I have no one else like him,[^19] who will genuinely care about your concerns.
οὐδένα γὰρ ἔχω ἰσόψυχον ὅστις γνησίως τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν μεριμνήσει,
For they all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
οἱ πάντες γὰρ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ζητοῦσιν, οὐ τὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
But you know his proven worth, how as a child with a father he has served[^20] with me in the good news.
τὴν δὲ δοκιμὴν αὐτοῦ γινώσκετε, ὅτι ὡς πατρὶ τέκνον σὺν ἐμοὶ ἐδούλευσεν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.
So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things go with me,
τοῦτον μὲν οὖν ἐλπίζω πέμψαι ὡς ἂν ἀφίδω τὰ περὶ ἐμὲ ἐξαυτῆς·
and I am confident in the Lord that I myself will also come soon.
πέποιθα δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ ὅτι καὶ αὐτὸς ταχέως ἐλεύσομαι.
But I have thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier, and your messenger[^21] and minister[^22] to my need,
Ἀναγκαῖον δὲ ἡγησάμην Ἐπαφρόδιτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν καὶ συνεργὸν καὶ συστρατιώτην μου, ὑμῶν δὲ ἀπόστολον καὶ λειτουργὸν τῆς χρείας μου, πέμψαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς,
for he has been longing for all of you,[^23] and has been distressed because you heard that he was ill.
ἐπειδὴ ἐπιποθῶν ἦν πάντας ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἀδημονῶν διότι ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἠσθένησεν.
Indeed he was ill, close to death. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but on me also, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.
καὶ γὰρ ἠσθένησεν παραπλήσιον θανάτῳ· ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς ἠλέησεν αὐτόν, οὐκ αὐτὸν δὲ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐμέ, ἵνα μὴ λύπην ἐπὶ λύπην σχῶ.
So I am sending[^24] him all the more eagerly, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less anxious.
σπουδαιοτέρως οὖν ἔπεμψα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἰδόντες αὐτὸν πάλιν χαρῆτε κἀγὼ ἀλυπότερος ὦ.
So welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and hold people like him in honor,
προσδέχεσθε οὖν αὐτὸν ἐν κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης χαρᾶς, καὶ τοὺς τοιούτους ἐντίμους ἔχετε,
because he came close to death for the work of Christ,[^25] risking his life to make up for what was lacking in your service to me.[^26]
ὅτι διὰ τὸ ἔργον Χριστοῦ μέχρι θανάτου ἤγγισεν, παραβολευσάμενος τῇ ψυχῇ ἵνα ἀναπληρώσῃ τὸ ὑμῶν ὑστέρημα τῆς πρός με λειτουργίας.

n.1: Greek *koinonia*, "sharing, fellowship". Or "fellowship with the Spirit", or "any common spirit".
n.5: Literally "not looking each to your own things, but also each to the things of others".
n.6: The second half of the verse has no verb. Or "which you also have in Christ Jesus", that is, the attitude that belongs to those who are in Christ. Many manuscripts read "For let this attitude be in you which was also in Christ Jesus".
n.7: Greek *morphe*, "form", the outward shape in which something appears; also in verse 7 ("the form of a servant"). How far the word also implies the nature of what appears is debated.
n.8: Or "though he was in the form of God", or "because he was in the form of God". The Greek participle allows either.
n.9: Greek *harpagmos*, a rare word, from *harpazo*, "to seize". It may mean something to be seized, which he did not yet have, or something already his, to be held on to or used for his own advantage.
n.10: Greek *ekenosen*, from *kenoo*, "to empty", also "to make of no account". The verse does not say of what he emptied himself; the phrases that follow describe what it involved.
n.12: Verses 10–11 echo Isaiah 45:23, where the LORD, God's personal name, says, "To me every knee will bow, every tongue will swear allegiance." The Septuagint has "every tongue will confess to God". *Lord*: Greek *kyrios*, the word the Greek Old Testament uses for the name YHWH.
n.18: Greek *leitourgia*, a public or priestly service; compare *leitourgos*, "minister", in verse 25, and verse 30.
n.21: Greek *apostolos*, "one who is sent", the word translated "apostle" elsewhere.
n.22: Greek *leitourgos*, one who performs a public or priestly service.
n.23: Some manuscripts read "longing to see all of you".
n.24: Literally "I sent", written from the point of view of the readers, who will receive the letter when Epaphroditus arrives.
n.25: Some manuscripts read "the work of the Lord".
n.26: Literally "to fill up your lack of service toward me". Greek *leitourgia*, as in verse 17.

v: Finally,[^1] my brothers and sisters,[^2] rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is no trouble for me, and it is a safeguard for you.
Τὸ λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί μου, χαίρετε ἐν κυρίῳ. τὰ αὐτὰ γράφειν ὑμῖν ἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρόν, ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλές.
Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the mutilation.[^3]
Βλέπετε τοὺς κύνας, βλέπετε τοὺς κακοὺς ἐργάτας, βλέπετε τὴν κατατομήν.
For we are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh,[^4]
ἡμεῖς γάρ ἐσμεν ἡ περιτομή, οἱ πνεύματι θεοῦ λατρεύοντες καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐν σαρκὶ πεποιθότες,
though I myself have reason for confidence in the flesh too. If anyone else thinks they have reason for confidence in the flesh, I have more:
καίπερ ἐγὼ ἔχων πεποίθησιν καὶ ἐν σαρκί. Εἴ τις δοκεῖ ἄλλος πεποιθέναι ἐν σαρκί, ἐγὼ μᾶλλον·
circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born of Hebrews;[^5] as to the Law, a Pharisee;
περιτομῇ ὀκταήμερος, ἐκ γένους Ἰσραήλ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, Ἑβραῖος ἐξ Ἑβραίων, κατὰ νόμον Φαρισαῖος,
as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to the righteousness that is in the Law, blameless.
κατὰ ζῆλος διώκων τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ γενόμενος ἄμεμπτος.
But whatever gains I had, these I have come to regard as loss because of Christ.
Ἀλλὰ ἅτινα ἦν μοι κέρδη, ταῦτα ἥγημαι διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν ζημίαν.

More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I regard them as rubbish,[^6] so that I may gain Christ
ἀλλὰ μενοῦνγε καὶ ἡγοῦμαι πάντα ζημίαν εἶναι διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου μου διʼ ὃν τὰ πάντα ἐζημιώθην, καὶ ἡγοῦμαι σκύβαλα ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω
and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the Law, but the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ,[^7] the righteousness from God that depends on faith,
καὶ εὑρεθῶ ἐν αὐτῷ, μὴ ἔχων ἐμὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ νόμου ἀλλὰ τὴν διὰ πίστεως Χριστοῦ, τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει,
that I may know him and the power of his resurrection and the sharing of his sufferings, being conformed to his death,
τοῦ γνῶναι αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ κοινωνίαν παθημάτων αὐτοῦ, συμμορφιζόμενος τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ,
if somehow I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.
εἴ πως καταντήσω εἰς τὴν ἐξανάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
Not that I have already obtained it or have already been made perfect,[^8] but I press on to take hold of it, because Christ[^9] has taken hold of me.[^10]
Οὐχ ὅτι ἤδη ἔλαβον ἢ ἤδη τετελείωμαι, διώκω δὲ εἰ καὶ καταλάβω, ἐφʼ ᾧ καὶ κατελήμφθην ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ.
Brothers and sisters, I do not[^11] consider that I have taken hold of it myself. But one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead,
ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ ἐμαυτὸν οὐ λογίζομαι κατειληφέναι· ἓν δέ, τὰ μὲν ὀπίσω ἐπιλανθανόμενος τοῖς δὲ ἔμπροσθεν ἐπεκτεινόμενος,
I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call[^12] of God in Christ Jesus.
κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω εἰς τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
So let those of us who are mature[^13] think this way. And if you think differently about anything, God will reveal that to you too.
ὅσοι οὖν τέλειοι, τοῦτο φρονῶμεν· καὶ εἴ τι ἑτέρως φρονεῖτε, καὶ τοῦτο ὁ θεὸς ὑμῖν ἀποκαλύψει·
Only let us keep in step with what we have already reached.[^14]
πλὴν εἰς ὃ ἐφθάσαμεν, τῷ αὐτῷ στοιχεῖν.
Brothers and sisters, join in imitating me, and watch those who live[^15] as we do, since you have us as an example.
Συμμιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, ἀδελφοί, καὶ σκοπεῖτε τοὺς οὕτω περιπατοῦντας καθὼς ἔχετε τύπον ἡμᾶς·
For many live, as I have often told you and now tell you even with tears, as enemies of the cross of Christ.
πολλοὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦσιν οὓς πολλάκις ἔλεγον ὑμῖν, νῦν δὲ καὶ κλαίων λέγω, τοὺς ἐχθροὺς τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
Their end is destruction, their god is their belly,[^16] and their glory is in their shame, with their minds set on earthly things.
ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια, ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία καὶ ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν, οἱ τὰ ἐπίγεια φρονοῦντες.
For our citizenship[^17] is in heaven, and from there we eagerly await a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
ἡμῶν γὰρ τὸ πολίτευμα ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὑπάρχει, ἐξ οὗ καὶ σωτῆρα ἀπεκδεχόμεθα κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν,
who will transform our lowly body[^18] to be like his glorious body, by the working of the power that enables him even to subject all things to himself.
ὃς μετασχηματίσει τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν σύμμορφον τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ δύνασθαι αὐτὸν καὶ ὑποτάξαι αὑτῷ τὰ πάντα.

n.1: Or "Furthermore". Greek *to loipon*, "as for the rest".
n.2: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike; also in verses 13 and 17.
n.3: Greek *katatome*, "cutting up, mutilation", a play on *peritome*, "circumcision", in verse 3.
n.4: Greek *sarx*, "flesh": here what is merely human and outward, such as the physical rite and the descent listed in verses 5–6; also in verse 4. Compare "the flesh" in Paul's moral sense, human nature in its weakness and opposition to God.
n.7: Or "through the faithfulness of Christ". Literally "through faith of Christ".
n.8: Or "have already reached the goal". Greek *teleioo*, "complete, make perfect".
n.9: The SBLGNT here follows Tregelles; other editions read "Christ Jesus".
n.10: Or "to take hold of that for which Christ took hold of me".
n.13: Greek *teleioi*, "mature, complete", from the same root as "made perfect" in verse 12.
n.14: Literally "Only, to what we have attained, keep in line by the same." Many manuscripts add "rule; let us think the same thing".
n.15: Literally "walk", a common biblical picture for a way of life; also in verse 18.
n.16: Or "stomach", that is, their own appetites.
n.17: Greek *politeuma*, "commonwealth, state, citizenship", related to the verb in 1:27.
n.18: Literally "the body of our humiliation". *His glorious body*: literally "the body of his glory".

v: Therefore, my brothers and sisters,[^1] whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, my beloved.
ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοὶ καὶ ἐπιπόθητοι, χαρὰ καὶ στέφανός μου, οὕτως στήκετε ἐν κυρίῳ, ἀγαπητοί.
I urge Euodia and I urge Syntyche to agree with each other[^2] in the Lord.
Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν κυρίῳ.

Yes, and I ask you too, true companion,[^3] help these women, who have struggled together with me in the good news, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.
ναὶ ἐρωτῶ καὶ σέ, γνήσιε σύζυγε, συλλαμβάνου αὐταῖς, αἵτινες ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ συνήθλησάν μοι μετὰ καὶ Κλήμεντος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου, ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐν βίβλῳ ζωῆς.
Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say, rejoice.
Χαίρετε ἐν κυρίῳ πάντοτε· πάλιν ἐρῶ, χαίρετε.
Let your gentleness[^4] be known to everyone. The Lord is near.[^5]
τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν γνωσθήτω πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις. ὁ κύριος ἐγγύς·
Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
μηδὲν μεριμνᾶτε, ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ δεήσει μετʼ εὐχαριστίας τὰ αἰτήματα ὑμῶν γνωριζέσθω πρὸς τὸν θεόν·
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
καὶ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ ὑπερέχουσα πάντα νοῦν φρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν καὶ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

Finally, brothers and sisters, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable, if there is any excellence and if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
Τὸ λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί, ὅσα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, ὅσα σεμνά, ὅσα δίκαια, ὅσα ἁγνά, ὅσα προσφιλῆ, ὅσα εὔφημα, εἴ τις ἀρετὴ καὶ εἴ τις ἔπαινος, ταῦτα λογίζεσθε·
What you have learned and received and heard and seen in me, practice these things. And the God of peace will be with you.
ἃ καὶ ἐμάθετε καὶ παρελάβετε καὶ ἠκούσατε καὶ εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοί, ταῦτα πράσσετε· καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθʼ ὑμῶν.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord that now at last you have revived your concern for me.[^6] You were indeed concerned, but you had no opportunity.
Ἐχάρην δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ μεγάλως ὅτι ἤδη ποτὲ ἀνεθάλετε τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν, ἐφʼ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ.
Not that I am speaking out of need, for I have learned to be content[^7] in whatever circumstances I am.
οὐχ ὅτι καθʼ ὑστέρησιν λέγω, ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔμαθον ἐν οἷς εἰμι αὐτάρκης εἶναι·
I know how to be brought low, and I know how to have plenty. In any and every circumstance I have learned the secret[^8] of being well fed and of going hungry, of having plenty and of being in need.
οἶδα καὶ ταπεινοῦσθαι, οἶδα καὶ περισσεύειν· ἐν παντὶ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν μεμύημαι, καὶ χορτάζεσθαι καὶ πεινᾶν, καὶ περισσεύειν καὶ ὑστερεῖσθαι·
I can do all things through him who strengthens me.[^9]
πάντα ἰσχύω ἐν τῷ ἐνδυναμοῦντί με.
Yet you did well to share with me in my trouble.
πλὴν καλῶς ἐποιήσατε συγκοινωνήσαντές μου τῇ θλίψει.
And you Philippians know yourselves that in the beginning of the good news, when I left Macedonia, no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving[^10] except you only,
Οἴδατε δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς, Φιλιππήσιοι, ὅτι ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ὅτε ἐξῆλθον ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας, οὐδεμία μοι ἐκκλησία ἐκοινώνησεν εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς μόνοι,
for even in Thessalonica you sent help for my need more than once.[^11]
ὅτι καὶ ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δὶς εἰς τὴν χρείαν μοι ἐπέμψατε.
Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that increases to your account.
οὐχ ὅτι ἐπιζητῶ τὸ δόμα, ἀλλὰ ἐπιζητῶ τὸν καρπὸν τὸν πλεονάζοντα εἰς λόγον ὑμῶν.
I have received full payment, and more. I am well supplied, now that I have received from Epaphroditus what you sent, a pleasing aroma,[^12] an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
ἀπέχω δὲ πάντα καὶ περισσεύω· πεπλήρωμαι δεξάμενος παρὰ Ἐπαφροδίτου τὰ παρʼ ὑμῶν, ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, θυσίαν δεκτήν, εὐάρεστον τῷ θεῷ.
And my God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
ὁ δὲ θεός μου πληρώσει πᾶσαν χρείαν ὑμῶν κατὰ τὸ πλοῦτος αὐτοῦ ἐν δόξῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
To our God and Father be the glory forever and ever.[^13] Amen.
τῷ δὲ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ ἡμῶν ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
Greet every one of God's holy people[^14] in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.[^15]
Ἀσπάσασθε πάντα ἅγιον ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ. ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ ἀδελφοί.
All God's holy people greet you, especially those of Caesar's household.[^16]
ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι, μάλιστα δὲ οἱ ἐκ τῆς Καίσαρος οἰκίας.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.[^17]
ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ὑμῶν.

n.1: Greek *adelphoi*, "brothers", used of the believers, men and women alike; also in verse 8.
n.3: Greek *syzygos*, "yokefellow, partner". It may also be a personal name: "true Syzygus".
n.5: Or "The Lord is close at hand".
n.6: Literally "you have blossomed again in thinking of me".
n.7: Greek *autarkes*, "self-sufficient", a word the Stoic philosophers used for a person not ruled by circumstances.
n.8: Greek *myeo*, "initiate", a word used of initiation into the mystery religions.
n.9: Many manuscripts read "through Christ who strengthens me".
n.10: Literally "in an account of giving and receiving", the language of business; also "account" in verse 17 and "received full payment" in verse 18.
n.12: Literally "a smell of fragrance", the language of the sacrifices in the Old Testament (Exodus 29:18; Leviticus 1:9).
n.13: Literally "to the ages of the ages".
n.14: Literally "every holy one", traditionally "every saint"; also "God's holy people" in verse 22.
n.15: Greek *adelphoi*, here Paul's companions; the word can include women.
n.16: That is, people in the emperor's service, whether slaves or freed slaves.
n.17: Many manuscripts read "be with you all. Amen."
